paragraphs: Hello, I am Lily, and I write for Explorers' Blog. Our school library has many signs. Mia, Leo, May, and I read them all during club hour on Thursday. This post tells you about five of them. Each sign helps the children in the library. New children can read this post before they come.

The first sign is on the door. It says, "LIBRARY. OPEN MONDAY TO FRIDAY. EIGHT O'CLOCK TO FOUR O'CLOCK." So the library is closed on Saturday and Sunday. The second sign is inside, next to the door. It says, "WHISPER, PLEASE." People read and work here, so we speak very quietly. Leo likes this sign, because he can whisper his funny stories.

The third sign is in the corner near the window. It says, "TALK CORNER. YOU CAN HAVE A CONVERSATION HERE." In this corner, children talk with their friends and make plans. Mia and May often sit there on soft cushions. The next sign is on a big table. It says, "PROJECT TABLE. PLEASE LEAVE IT CLEAN." The Explorers use this table for posters and maps. After they finish, they clean the table.

The last sign is above a shelf in the middle of the room. It says, "NEW AND INTERESTING BOOKS. LOOK ON THE MIDDLE SHELF." Mia found an unusual book there about sea animals. It has many big pictures of fish. You can also borrow a book for one week. May writes the name of her book on a small card. Then she gives the card to the person at the desk.

These signs are small, but they are important. If you read them, the library is quiet, clean, and friendly. Do you have signs in your school? Which sign do you like best? Write to us, and tell us about it. We hope to see you in our library soon. Lily
